A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable matching despite v2's added experiments and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning and projection experiments, utility and harmfulness measurements, and analyses of weight and activation subspace overlap.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments using safety-tuned Llama models, reported in Figures 6–8 and Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: V2 extends the procedure with targeted safety tuning, producing WS and the safety-specific update ΔS = WS−W0. Downstream fine-tuning and projection can now start from WS instead of WA. This adds an alternative subspace construction while retaining the SVD, projection, and overlap procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds harmless-response/refusal training using BeaverTails entries labeled is_safe=True. This introduces a distinct training population and task within an existing dataset. The MetaMathQA, GSM8K, harmful BeaverTails, AdvBench, MATH, and ToxiGen coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Random-K and Random remain the projection comparison methods, and MSO retains the analytic random-subspace baseline. V2 applies these controls to safety-tuned starting models, with corresponding unprojected checkpoint references; it introduces no additional competing projection or defense method.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation configurations starting from safety-tuned Llama-3.2 1B and Llama-2 7B checkpoints. Its additional weight-overlap analysis uses three layer selections in Figure 8. Existing dataset sizes, contamination proportion, evaluation metrics, activation sampling, and fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 6–8 add a substantial test of candidate-subspace dependence: whether targeted safety-tuning updates behave differently from general alignment updates. V2 examines their projection effects, contaminated-update filtering, and pairwise weight-space overlap. This addresses an alternative explanation for v1's findings; the activation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. Averaging harmfulness across prompts, averaging activation overlap across layers, and the analytic random-subspace expectation are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing table results are retained apart from equivalent rounding. V2 adds safety-tuned Llama results across pure and contaminated fine-tuning, plus new overlap curves. For example, Table 4 reports Llama-2 7B fine-tuned utility of 0.151 and harmfulness of 3.84 in the respective full-useful and full-harmful settings. These are new experimental conditions, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The SVD subspace construction, projection operators, energy-kept ratio, MSO definition, and random-subspace expectation retain the same mathematics. V2 applies these definitions to the additional safety-tuned update through expanded notation; it adds no distinct mathematical argument, formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly narrows the headline scope to linear subspaces and extends the central contribution to safety-specific updates, beyond general alignment updates. It also strengthens v1's evidence-based conclusion into claims that the experiments establish linear non-separability and confirm that no weight-space region can isolate safety.

C2.justification: V2 extends the general-learning interpretation to safety-specific updates and discusses their stronger overlap with useful than harmful updates. Its limitations replace v1's explicit small/mid-sized-model and alternative-alignment generalization concerns with an open-weight versus closed-source boundary. The nonlinear limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the is_safe=True filtering instruction for the new safety-tuning stage and explicitly states that the existing hyperparameter configuration also applies to safety tuning. Hardware, precision, software libraries, optimizer settings, and the public code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 retains the earlier references and adds four works concerning safety neurons, mechanistic safety fine-tuning, template-region safety mechanisms, and multidimensional safety directions. Related work gains corresponding discussion, while the introduction more explicitly distinguishes alignment-derived and targeted-safety-derived subspaces.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and numerous explanatory paragraphs are substantially rewritten. V2 standardizes activation-space terminology, reorganizes the appendices, moves experimental details earlier and limitations out of the main text, and adds appendix contents and an LLM-writing-assistance disclosure.

P2.justification: V2 adds three multipanel figures and expands two appendix result tables with safety-tuned model blocks. Figure 1 incorporates the additional training route, Figure 4 changes labels and baseline markers, and the former appendix Figure 6 becomes Figure 9. Typography, figure placement, and appendix layout are also revised.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful test of an important ambiguity in v1: general alignment updates mix safety with other capabilities. The targeted safety-tuning experiments provide additional evidence, and the title's linear qualification better matches the analysis. The gain remains limited: the new results cover two Llama models, while the strengthened non-separability claims exceed what testing these candidate constructions establishes, and the revised limitations omit the earlier model-size caveat.
